chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: When a person reaches forty years, God the Exalted protects him from three diseases: insanity, leprosy, and vitiligo. When he reaches fifty, God eases his reckoning. When he reaches sixty, God grants him repentance. When he reaches seventy, the people of heaven love him. When he reaches eighty, God orders the recording of his good deeds and the casting away of his bad deeds. When he reaches ninety, God forgives him what preceded of his sin and what followed, and records him as a captive of God in His land. And in another tradition: When he reaches one hundred, that is the lowest stage of life, and it is narrated that the lowest stage of life is when his intellect is like that of a seven-year-old child.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of reaching the ages of forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, and ninety according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a spiritual roadmap where aging is not merely physical decline but a progressive elevation of the soul, culminating in divine favor and the 'lowest stage of life' (arzhal al-'umur) characterized by the return of childlike innocence rather than mere senility. This narrative reflects the Shia emphasis on *tadarru'* (humble submission) and the purification of the heart through the accumulation of years, linking biological aging to metaphysical maturity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 22-25 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Muqayrih that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) quoted on the authority of the Prophet (MGB), “The Honorable the Exalted God will protect anyone who attains the age of forty from three diseases: insanity, vitiligo and leprosy . God will ease the Reckoning of anyone who reachesthe age of fifty. God will grant anyone who reaches the age of sixty opportunity to repent. The companions of the heavens love anyone who reaches the age of seventy. God will order the good deeds to be recorded, and the bad deeds to be eliminated for anyone who reaches the age of eighty. Whenever a man reaches the age of ninety, God will forgive all his past and future sins. He will be considered to be one of the slaves of God on Earth.”In another tradition we read, “When he reaches the age of one-hundred he has reached the worst age.”In another tradition we read, “When one reaches his worst age, his intellect is like that of a seven year old child.”
